overview.h1: HTS Chapter 79: Zinc and Articles Thereof — 2026 Tariff Rates

seo.title: HTS Chapter 79 Zinc Tariffs: Zinc HS Codes, Import Duty Rates & 2026 Section 301 | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Searchable U.S. duty table for all 13 HTS Chapter 79 zinc lines: unwrought zinc ingots 1.5% to 3% (Free under USMCA and FTAs, no Section 232), zinc scrap Free, zinc dust, wire, sheet and articles. 2026 Section 301 on 6 lines, China 25% to 41.7%.

overview.intro:
Chapter 79 covers zinc from the smelter to finished zinc articles: **unwrought zinc** (special high grade and casting-grade zinc, and zinc alloy ingots, 7901), **zinc scrap** (7902), **zinc dust, powders and flakes** (7903), **bars, rods and wire** (7904), **plates, sheet, strip and foil** (7905) and **other articles of zinc** such as anodes, die castings and fittings (7907). Base rates are low: Free to 4.2%, and Free under USMCA and every U.S. free trade agreement.

Zinc has **no Section 232 duty**. It is on the 2025 U.S. critical minerals list, but Proclamation 11001 (January 14, 2026) chose negotiations, not tariffs, for processed critical minerals. The extra duty that matters is the **2026 Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** (10% or 12.5%, from July 24, 2026): unwrought zinc, scrap, zinc powder and the 'other articles' line are on its exemption list (note 52(b)), so it reaches only 6 of the 13 lines (zinc dust and flakes, bars and wire, sheet, household articles and tubes). **USMCA-qualifying goods of Canada and Mexico pay none of it**, and Canada's 2026 Section 338 duties list no zinc. China pays 25% on unwrought zinc and on most zinc products (Section 301), and Brazil 37.5% on the six non-exempt lines.

No antidumping or countervailing duty order covers Chapter 79 goods.

productGroups.label: Unwrought zinc & zinc alloys
productGroups.blurb: Zinc metal as cast: special high grade (SHG) zinc of 99.99% or more (7901.11), casting-grade zinc (7901.12.10) and other unalloyed zinc, plus unwrought zinc alloys such as die-casting alloy ingots (7901.20): 4 lines at 1.5% or 3%, Free under USMCA and every U.S. FTA. On the 2026 Section 301 exemption list; China pays 25% (note 31(b)).

productGroups.label: Zinc waste & scrap
productGroups.blurb: Zinc and zinc-alloy waste and scrap, such as die-cast scrap, old zinc and new clippings: 1 line, Free. It pays no extra duty from any country today: it is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list and on no China list. Zinc dross and skimmings are Chapter 26 (2620.19.30).

productGroups.label: Zinc dust, powders & flakes
productGroups.blurb: Zinc dust made by condensing zinc vapor (7903.10, 0.7¢/kg), zinc powders (7903.90.30, 0.5¢/kg) and zinc flakes (7903.90.60, 3%), used in zinc-rich paints, batteries and chemicals. Zinc powder is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list; zinc dust and flakes are not.

productGroups.label: Zinc bars, rods, profiles & wire
productGroups.blurb: Zinc bars, rods, profiles and wire, including zinc wire for thermal spraying (metallizing) and extruded anode rod: 1 line at 4.2%, the highest base rate in the chapter. Pays the 2026 Section 301 duty.

productGroups.label: Zinc plates, sheets, strip & foil
productGroups.blurb: Rolled zinc plate, sheet, strip and foil, including titanium-zinc roofing and cladding sheet and battery-can strip: 1 line at 2.8%. Pays the 2026 Section 301 duty. Galvanized (zinc-coated) steel sheet is Chapter 72, not 79.

productGroups.label: Other articles of zinc
productGroups.blurb: Household, table, kitchen and sanitary articles of zinc (7907.00.10), zinc tubes, pipes and fittings (7907.00.20) and all other zinc articles (7907.00.60): sacrificial anodes, die-cast zinc hardware, keychains and fittings: 3 lines at 3%. 7907.00.60 is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list; China pays 25% on it (List 3).

workedExamples.title: $1,000,000 of SHG zinc ingots from Canada
workedExamples.body: Special high grade zinc (99.99% or more) is 1.5%, **Free** with a USMCA claim. It is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list (note 52(b), 9903.05.86), outside Section 232, and on none of Canada's Section 338 lists, so the duty is **$0**. Without a USMCA claim it is $15,000 (1.5%), still with no extra duty.

workedExamples.title: Zinc slab from Peru or Australia
workedExamples.body: Unalloyed zinc under 99.99% (not casting grade) is 1.5%, **Free** under the U.S.–Peru TPA (PE) or the U.S.–Australia FTA (AU). The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on Peru (9903.05.63) and Australia (9903.05.23) does not apply to unwrought zinc (note 52(b)), so an FTA claim makes the duty **$0**.

workedExamples.title: Zinc sheet from Germany or Spain (EU)
workedExamples.body: Zinc plate and sheet is 2.8%. The EU's 2026 Section 301 rate (9903.05.39) sets the total at **10%** when the base rate is lower, so the 2.8% is replaced by 10%: **$10,000 on $100,000** instead of $2,800 before July 24, 2026.

workedExamples.title: Zinc alloy sacrificial anodes from China
workedExamples.body: CBP ruling N300700 classified die-cast zinc anodes for boats in 7907.00.60 (3%). China pays **+25%** under Section 301 List 3 (9903.88.03) = **28%**. The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on China does not apply because 7907.00.60 is on the note 52(b) exemption list. Zinc ribbon anodes with a steel core went to 8543.30 instead (N271791).

workedExamples.title: Zinc wire for thermal spraying from China
workedExamples.body: 4.2% base **+ 25%** List 3 (9903.88.03) **+ 12.5%** 2026 Section 301 (9903.05.31; note 52(a) keeps the China lists on top) = **41.7%**: $41,700 on $100,000. The same wire from Mexico with USMCA is Free.

workedExamples.title: Zinc scrap from Mexico
workedExamples.body: Zinc waste and scrap is **Free** and on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, so it pays **no duty** with or without a USMCA claim. Processed zinc scrap being recycled is also excluded from EPA's hazardous-waste rules (40 CFR 261.4(a)(13)).

notes.chapterNotes: **Subheading note 1 (definitions).** (a) *Zinc, not alloyed*: metal containing by weight at least 97.5% zinc. (b) *Zinc alloys*: metallic substances in which zinc predominates by weight over each other element, provided the other elements total more than 2.5% by weight. (c) *Zinc dust*: dust obtained by condensation of zinc vapor, of spherical particles finer than zinc powders; at least 80% by weight must pass a 63-micrometer sieve, and it must contain at least 85% metallic zinc.
notes.additionalUsNotes: **1.** For heading 7901, *casting-grade zinc* contains at least 97.5% zinc and one or more of: more than 1.8% lead, more than 1.8% cadmium, more than 1.8% iron, more than 0.5% aluminum, more than 1% copper, more than 0.08% titanium, or more than 0.1% of any other base metal taken separately. Casting-grade zinc (7901.12.10) is 3%; other zinc under 99.99% (7901.12.50) is 1.5%.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 79 Tariff Updates: Zinc Tariffs 2025–2026

seo.title: Zinc Tariff Updates 2026: Section 301 on 60 Economies, USMCA, China, No Section 232 (HTS Ch. 79) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Every change to U.S. tariffs on zinc (HTS Chapter 79) since January 2025, with official sources: the 2026 Section 301 duties and their unwrought-zinc exemption, the USMCA exemption, China's 25% on unwrought zinc, the end of the IEEPA and Section 122 tariffs, Canada's Section 338 lists and the critical minerals proclamation.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule, the **2025 Basic Edition** (in force January 1, 2025) and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026), and lists every extra duty that reaches Chapter 79 today. Base rates did not change: all 13 lines carry the same general rate in both editions.

The extra duties did change. The IEEPA tariffs of 2025 ended on **February 24, 2026** and the Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on **July 23, 2026**; unwrought zinc, scrap and zinc powder were exempt from both. Since **July 24, 2026** the **2026 Section 301 duties on 60 economies** (10% or 12.5%) apply to the six zinc lines that are not on the note 52(b) exemption list, with USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico exempt. China's Section 301 duties stack on top: **25%** on unwrought zinc since September 27, 2024 and 25% on most zinc products since 2019.

Zinc is **not** a Section 232 metal: Proclamation 11001 (January 14, 2026) answered the processed critical minerals investigation with negotiations, not tariffs. Canada's 2026 Section 338 lists contain no Chapter 79 line, and no antidumping or countervailing duty order covers Chapter 79 goods.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 79 from any country: China Section 301 (note 20 lists and the note 31 2024 increases), the 2026 Section 301 actions on 60 economies and Brazil (notes 52, 50), Russia's column 2 rates, the scheduled Nicaragua Section 301 duty (note 29), and the ended IEEPA and Section 122 duties. No Section 232 note (16 and 19 metals, 33 and 38 vehicle parts, 36/37 wood, 39 semiconductors) lists a Chapter 79 line; Canada's Section 338 lists (note 51) contain none; and Commerce has no antidumping or countervailing duty order on Chapter 79 products. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods entered free under USMCA pay none of it (9903.05.93, note 52(g)), Free lines included. Note 52(b) (9903.05.86) exempts 7 of the 13 lines for every country: unwrought zinc and zinc alloys (all 4 lines of 7901), zinc scrap (7902), zinc powders (7903.90.30) and other articles of zinc (7907.00.60). The duty reaches only zinc dust (7903.10), flakes (7903.90.60), bars, rods and wire (7904), plates and sheet (7905), household articles (7907.00.10) and tubes and fittings (7907.00.20). Canada's 2026 Section 338 duties (note 51) list no Chapter 79 line, and the IEEPA duty on Canada ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: No Chapter 79 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 13 Chapter 79 lines carry the same general rate in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; none changed and none are new or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 duties continue during the review
changes.detail: USTR announced that the 2018–2019 Section 301 actions on China, including List 3 (25%) on seven Chapter 79 lines, continue while the statutory four-year review proceeds. The 25% on unwrought zinc (note 31(b)) is unaffected.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duties: no Chapter 79 line
changes.detail: Proclamations 11046–11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.12–9903.03.14) on Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy products and motor vehicles listed in note 51(b), from August 22, 2026. No Chapter 79 line is on any of the lists, so Canadian zinc pays only its base rate (Free with USMCA).

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies reach 6 zinc lines
changes.detail: The 10% or 12.5% duties on goods of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) took effect. Note 52(b) exempts unwrought zinc and alloys, scrap, zinc powders and 7907.00.60 for every country, so only zinc dust and flakes, bars, rods and wire, sheet, household articles and tubes pay. USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt (notes 52(g), 52(h)); the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan pay a total of 10% or 12.5% in place of the base rate; the China lists stack on top (note 52(a)).

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026. Unwrought zinc, scrap, zinc powders and 7907.00.60 were on its product exemption list (9903.03.03), and USMCA goods were exempt (9903.03.07, 9903.03.08).

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Brazil reaches the same 6 zinc lines
changes.detail: The 25% duty on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) took effect. Note 50(a)(ii) (9903.05.03) exempts unwrought zinc, scrap, zinc powders and 7907.00.60, the same lines note 52(b) exempts, so Brazilian zinc sheet, wire, dust and household articles pay 25% plus the 12.5% 2026 duty.

changes.title: USTR opens the second four-year review of the China duties
changes.detail: USTR started the second statutory four-year review of the 2018 Section 301 actions on China, which include List 3 and the 2024 increase on unwrought zinc.

changes.title: USTR seeks comments on a critical minerals trade agreement
changes.detail: Following Proclamation 11001, USTR asked for comments (by March 19, 2026) on a plurilateral agreement on trade in critical minerals, including minimum prices or other price mechanisms with border measures, and on keeping scrap metal flowing into domestic production. No tariff on zinc has resulted as of October 13, 2026.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: A 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) applied until July 23, 2026. In Chapter 79 it reached only the six lines outside its exemption list (9903.03.03): zinc dust and flakes, bars and wire, sheet, household articles and tubes. USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Critical minerals Section 232: negotiations, no tariff
changes.detail: Proclamation 11001 concurred with Commerce that imports of processed critical minerals and their derivative products threaten national security, but directed Commerce and USTR to negotiate agreements (considering price floors) rather than impose tariffs, with an update due within 180 days and other measures possible later. No duty on zinc was imposed.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29), on every Chapter 79 line. The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: Zinc added to the U.S. critical minerals list
changes.detail: The U.S. Geological Survey's final 2025 List of Critical Minerals includes zinc. The list feeds the Section 232 critical minerals work but does not itself change any tariff.

changes.title: Section 232 investigation of processed critical minerals opens
changes.detail: Executive Order 14272 directed Commerce to investigate imports of processed critical minerals and derivative products; Commerce asked for public comments on April 25, 2025. It ended with Proclamation 11001 (negotiations, no tariff).

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff: unwrought zinc and scrap exempt
changes.detail: Executive Order 14257 set the reciprocal tariffs from April 5, 2025, with an Annex II exemption list (9903.01.32) that, as printed in the current schedule, covers unwrought zinc and alloys, zinc scrap, zinc powders and 7907.00.60. The other zinc lines paid the country's reciprocal rate. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada (9903.01.10) and Mexico (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025; USMCA goods were exempted from March 7, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China: 25% on unwrought zinc (2024 four-year review)
changes.detail: USTR's four-year review raised duties on Chinese critical minerals. Unwrought zinc and zinc alloys (7901.11, 7901.12.10, 7901.12.50, 7901.20), which were on no earlier list, pay 25% under heading 9903.91.01 (note 31(b)).

changes.title: China List 3 raised to 25%
changes.detail: The List 3 duty on Chinese zinc dust, powders and flakes, bars and wire, sheet, tubes and other zinc articles (7903, 7904, 7905, 7907.00.20, 7907.00.60), 10% from September 24, 2018, rose to 25%.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 79 zinc were **$2.48B in 2025**, +13.4% from $2.19B in 2024, below the 2022 peak of $3.14B. **Unwrought zinc (7901) was $2.07B, 83% of the total**, and special high grade zinc of 99.99% or more (7901.11) alone was $1.27B (+30%). Canada supplied $1.21B (49%), almost all of it zinc metal ($1.17B); Mexico $318M and Peru $299M (+52%) also shipped mainly unwrought zinc, and Australia rose from $26M to $187M. These are the goods on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, and from USMCA and FTA partners they enter Free.

Other articles of zinc (7907) were $316M (+8%), led by China ($137M, nearly all of China's $140M), Taiwan ($45M) and India ($26M). Zinc dust, powders and flakes were $55M (Belgium $30M), scrap $17M, bars, rods and wire $17M and sheet $9M. The 2026 Section 301 duties fall on parts of these smaller groups.

2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Zinc ores and concentrates (Chapter 26) and zinc oxide (Chapter 28) are not included. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duties for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. For **unwrought zinc and zinc scrap**, which are 85% of U.S. zinc imports, the answer is simple: no extra duty except from China, so the total is the 1.5% or 3% base rate, or Free under USMCA and the Peru, Australia, Korea and other FTAs.

For **zinc dust and flakes, wire, sheet, household articles and tubes**, the 2026 Section 301 duties add 10% or 12.5% for 60 economies (a flat 10% or 12.5% total for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan), even when an FTA rate is claimed, except for USMCA-qualifying goods of Canada and Mexico. China pays 25% to 37.5% extra and Brazil 37.5%. No antidumping or countervailing duty applies to Chapter 79 goods.

assumptions: Each total was computed by the official-measures calculator engine (the same data as the tariff calculator: measures.json, HTSUS 2026 Revision 21) for goods entered on 2026-10-13, priced on a $10,000 shipment and 1,000 units for per-unit rates.
Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
A per-unit rate plus a percentage cannot be added into one number without the shipment’s weight, count or volume, so it is shown as written.

Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; PE for Peru; AU for Australia; KR for South Korea. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

No Section 232 duty is shown because none reaches Chapter 79. The Section 232 automobile and MHDV parts elections (notes 33, 38) can reach zinc parts only when the importer certifies them as vehicle parts; that opt-in election is not applied.
The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied.
No antidumping or countervailing duty order covers Chapter 79 goods. Zinc-coated (galvanized) steel products are Chapters 72 and 73 and carry their own orders there.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 79: Zinc and Articles Thereof — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Zinc: HS Codes, USMCA Claims, TSCA, Hazmat & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 79) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 79 zinc line: USMCA and FTA claims, the note 52(b) Section 301 exemption for unwrought zinc and scrap, CBP classification rulings for zinc anodes and keychains, TSCA import certification, zinc dust hazmat rules, EPA scrap rules and marking, plus the legal ways to pay less.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For zinc the classification decides whether the 2026 Section 301 duty applies. Unwrought zinc and zinc alloys (7901), scrap (7902), zinc powders (7903.90.30) and other articles of zinc (7907.00.60) are on the note 52(b) exemption list; zinc dust, flakes, bars and wire, sheet, household articles and tubes are not. Origin decides the rest: USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico pay no Section 301 duty at all, while Chinese zinc pays 25% or more.

The legal ways to pay less: claim USMCA or an FTA, classify the product correctly (with a CBP ruling when unsure), avoid Chinese and Brazilian origin for covered lines, and use drawback on re-exported goods. Entry rules add TSCA certification for zinc metal and powders, hazmat rules for zinc dust, and EPA's scrap-metal exclusion for zinc scrap. Each rule and lever links to its regulation.

levers.title: Claim USMCA for Canadian and Mexican zinc
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 4.2%) and the whole 10% 2026 Section 301 duty
levers.appliesTo: All 13 lines, for goods of Canada and Mexico that qualify under the USMCA rules of origin
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin by the importer, exporter or producer (19 CFR 182.12), kept on file and produced when CBP asks.
levers.caveat: Only goods entered free under USMCA (SPI S/S+) get the Section 301 exemption (notes 52(g), 52(h)); non-qualifying goods pay base + 10% on the six covered lines.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(g)–(h)

levers.title: Claim the FTA rate for the base duty
levers.saves: The base rate: 1.5% or 3% on unwrought zinc, 0.5¢ to 0.7¢/kg on dust and powder, up to 4.2% on wire
levers.appliesTo: Originating goods of Peru (PE), Australia (AU), Korea (KR), Chile (CL), Colombia (CO), CAFTA-DR (P) and the other FTA partners in the Special column
levers.document: The agreement's certification or proof of origin (Peru: 19 CFR 10.3004), kept on file and presented when CBP asks.
levers.caveat: Note 52(a): an FTA claim does not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty, so it saves the most on unwrought zinc, scrap and the other exempt lines, where it makes the duty $0.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Classify the zinc form and product correctly
levers.saves: The 10% to 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty when a product is truly unwrought zinc, scrap, powder or a 7907.00.60 article, and the 1.5-point gap between casting-grade (3%) and other zinc (1.5%)
levers.appliesTo: All lines; most often unwrought vs wrought shapes, zinc dust (subheading note 1(c)) vs powders, casting-grade zinc (additional U.S. note 1), and 7907.00.60 vs other headings for anodes and keychains
levers.document: Chemical analysis and particle-size data (chapter notes), a description of form and use and, if unsure, a CBP binding ruling.
levers.caveat: Classification follows the product, not the duty: CBP put die-cast zinc anodes in 7907.00.60 (N300700) and zinc keychains in 7907.00.60 (N347980), but steel-cored zinc ribbon anodes in 8543.30 (N271791). Zinc oxide is 2817.00 and zinc dross and skimmings 2620.19.30, outside Chapter 79.

levers.title: Avoid Chinese and Brazilian origin for covered lines
levers.saves: 25% on unwrought zinc and up to 37.5% on zinc wire, sheet, dust and tubes from China; 37.5% on the six covered lines from Brazil
levers.appliesTo: Goods of China (12 of 13 lines) and Brazil (6 lines)
levers.document: Mill certificates and production records showing where the zinc was smelted, rolled, drawn or cast. Origin follows the last substantial transformation; ask CBP for a ruling if processing happens in more than one country.
levers.caveat: Remelting or simple processing in a third country may not change origin. Other countries still pay 10% or 12.5% on the six covered lines.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 31 and 50

levers.title: Drawback on zinc that is exported or used in exports
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the base rate and Section 301 duties paid
levers.appliesTo: All lines, for zinc re-exported or used to make exported products (for example galvanized steel or die castings)
levers.document: A drawback claim to CBP with import, manufacturing and export records (19 CFR part 191).
levers.caveat: Claims must meet the deadlines and records rules of part 191; goods of Canada and Mexico have USMCA drawback limits.

rules.title: 2026 Section 301: report the country's 9903.05.20–9903.05.84 heading on the six covered lines, or 9903.05.86 (note 52(b)) / 9903.05.93–.94 (USMCA) when exempt; China also reports 9903.88.03 or 9903.91.01

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 31 and 52

rules.title: TSCA import certification for zinc metal and zinc dust, powders and flakes as chemical substances in bulk; particles are never 'articles', and zinc sheet, wire or finished articles need it only if a TSCA rule requires
Zinc powder or zinc dust is a hazardous material (UN1436, Division 4.3, dangerous when wet, subsidiary 4.2): hazmat packaging, labels and shipping papers for transport from the port
Processed zinc scrap being recycled is excluded from the definition of solid waste, and other scrap metal is exempt from the hazardous-waste rules, so no RCRA import notice applies
Country of origin marking on the article or its container; zinc ingots, slabs, bars, plates, sheets, wire and scrap are on the J-list, but their outermost container must be marked
Binding classification rulings: zinc alloy sacrificial anodes 7907.00.60 (N300700), zinc keychains 7907.00.60 (N347980), steel-cored zinc ribbon anodes 8543.30 (N271791)

groups.label: Unwrought zinc & zinc alloys
groups.note: On the 2026 Section 301 exemption list: base rate only (1.5% or 3%), Free under USMCA and the FTAs. China 26.5% to 28% (note 31(b)). Casting-grade zinc is defined in additional U.S. note 1.

groups.label: Zinc waste & scrap
groups.note: Free and on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, on no China list: no extra duty from any country except column 2 rates. Zinc dross and skimmings are 2620.19.30.

groups.label: Zinc dust, powders & flakes
groups.note: Zinc dust (7903.10) and flakes (7903.90.60) pay the 2026 Section 301 duty; zinc powders (7903.90.30) are exempt. Zinc dust is UN1436 hazmat.

groups.label: Zinc bars, rods, profiles & wire
groups.note: 4.2% base + 10% or 12.5% 2026 Section 301 (flat 10% or 12.5% for the EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan). Free with USMCA. China 41.7%.

groups.label: Zinc plates, sheets, strip & foil
groups.note: 2.8% base + 10% or 12.5% 2026 Section 301. Free with USMCA. China 40.3%. Galvanized steel sheet is Chapter 72.

groups.label: Other articles of zinc
groups.note: Household articles and tubes pay the 2026 Section 301 duty; other articles (7907.00.60: anodes, die castings, keychains) are exempt. China 15.5% to 40.5%.

finalConclusion.h1: HTS Chapter 79 FAQ: Zinc Tariffs, HS Codes and Exemptions

seo.title: Zinc Tariff FAQ 2026: Is There a Tariff on Zinc? HS Codes for Ingots, Alloy, Anodes, Dust, Scrap (HTS Ch. 79) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about U.S. zinc tariffs and HS codes: zinc ingots, zinc alloy, anodes, keychains, zinc dust and scrap, Section 232, critical minerals, China and Canada, and where U.S. zinc imports come from.
keywords: is there a tariff on zinc

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most-searched questions about U.S. tariffs and HS codes for zinc, by product and by country. Each answer links to the page with the detail and the official sources.
keyTakeaways: Unwrought zinc (1.5% or 3%) and zinc scrap (Free) pay no extra duty except from China: they are on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, and Free under USMCA and every U.S. FTA.

The 2026 Section 301 duties (10% or 12.5%, from July 24, 2026) reach only six lines: zinc dust and flakes, bars, rods and wire, sheet, household articles and tubes. USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt.
Zinc has no Section 232 duty: Proclamation 11001 chose negotiations for critical minerals. Canada's Section 338 duties list no zinc, and no AD/CVD order covers Chapter 79.
China pays 25% on unwrought zinc and up to 41.7% on zinc products. In 2025 the U.S. imported $2.48B of Chapter 79 goods, Canada ($1.21B) first.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on zinc imported into the U.S.?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on zinc
faqs.answer: Yes, but it is low for zinc metal. Unwrought zinc pays 1.5% (special high grade and other zinc) or 3% (casting-grade zinc and zinc alloys), and is Free under USMCA and every U.S. FTA; zinc scrap is Free. These goods are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties. Zinc dust and flakes, wire, sheet, household articles and tubes pay 0.5¢/kg to 4.2% plus 10% or 12.5% for 60 economies. China pays 25% or more.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for zinc?
faqs.answer: Zinc is HS Chapter 79. Unwrought zinc is 7901 (7901.11 for zinc of 99.99% or more, 7901.12 below that, 7901.20 for alloys), scrap 7902, dust, powders and flakes 7903, bars, rods and wire 7904, plates and sheet 7905 and other zinc articles 7907 (heading 7906 is not used in the U.S. schedule). Zinc ores are 2608.00 and zinc oxide 2817.00.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for zinc ingots (SHG zinc)?
faqs.answer: Special high grade (SHG) zinc ingots of at least 99.99% zinc are 7901.11.00.00, 1.5%, Free under USMCA and the FTAs. Zinc under 99.99% is 7901.12: casting-grade zinc (more than 1.8% lead, cadmium or iron, 0.5% aluminum, 1% copper, and so on) is 7901.12.10 at 3%, other zinc 7901.12.50 at 1.5%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for zinc alloy?
faqs.answer: Unwrought zinc alloy, such as die-casting alloy ingot, is 7901.20.00.00 at 3% (Free under USMCA and the FTAs) and exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties; Chinese zinc alloy pays 28%. Finished zinc alloy articles are classified by what they are: 7907.00.60 for most other zinc articles, unless a more specific heading in another chapter applies.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a zinc alloy keychain?
faqs.answer: CBP classified spin-cast zinc alloy keychains (a zinc alloy ornament with a steel split ring) in 7907.00.60.00, 3%, in ruling N347980 (2025). 7907.00.60 is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list; Chinese keychains of this kind pay 28% (List 3).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for zinc anodes?
faqs.answer: Die-cast zinc alloy sacrificial anodes for boats are 7907.00.60.00 (3%), per CBP ruling N300700, which rejected classification as engine parts. Zinc ribbon anodes with a steel core, for pipelines and tanks, were classified in 8543.30.00 (2.6%) in ruling N271791.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for zinc dust and zinc powder?
faqs.answer: Zinc dust (condensed from zinc vapor, at least 80% passing a 63-micrometer sieve, at least 85% metallic zinc) is 7903.10.00 at 0.7¢/kg; zinc powders are 7903.90.30 at 0.5¢/kg; flakes 7903.90.60 at 3%. Zinc powder is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties, zinc dust is not. Zinc dust ships as hazmat UN1436.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for zinc scrap?
faqs.answer: Zinc waste and scrap is 7902.00.00.00, Free. It is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list and on no China list, so it pays no extra duty from any country except column 2 rates (11%). Zinc dross and skimmings are 2620.19.30 (Chapter 26), also Free.

faqs.question: Is zinc subject to Section 232 tariffs?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on zinc
faqs.answer: No. The Section 232 metals duties cover steel, aluminum and copper, and no Chapter 79 line is in their lists. Zinc was part of the 2025 Section 232 investigation of processed critical minerals, but Proclamation 11001 (January 14, 2026) directed negotiations, not tariffs, and no zinc duty has followed as of October 13, 2026.

faqs.question: Is zinc a critical mineral in the U.S.?
searchedAs: are lead and zinc critical minerals
are copper and zinc critical minerals
faqs.answer: Yes. The U.S. Geological Survey's final 2025 List of Critical Minerals (90 FR 50494, November 7, 2025) includes zinc. Being on the list does not by itself add a tariff; China's Section 301 duty on unwrought zinc (25% since September 27, 2024) came from USTR's critical minerals increases.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on zinc from China?
faqs.answer: Chinese unwrought zinc pays 26.5% to 28% (base + 25%, note 31(b)). Zinc flakes, wire, sheet and tubes pay base + 25% (List 3) + 12.5% (2026 Section 301): 40.3% to 41.7%; zinc dust 0.7¢/kg + 37.5%. Other zinc articles (7907.00.60) pay 28%, household articles 15.5%, and zinc scrap is Free.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on zinc from Canada?
faqs.answer: Not for USMCA-qualifying zinc: every Chapter 79 line is Free under USMCA, and USMCA goods are exempt from the 10% 2026 Section 301 duty. Canada's 2026 Section 338 duties cover alcoholic beverages, dairy products and motor vehicles, not zinc. The 25% IEEPA duty ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. get its zinc?
searchedAs: where does the us get zinc
faqs.answer: In 2025 the U.S. imported $2.48B of Chapter 79 zinc products, 83% of it unwrought zinc. The largest suppliers were Canada $1.21B, Mexico $318M, Peru $299M, Australia $187M, China $140M. Zinc ores and concentrates (Chapter 26) are not included.

faqs.question: What is HTS Chapter 79?
faqs.answer: Chapter 79 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule covers zinc and articles of zinc: unwrought zinc and alloys, scrap, dust and powders, bars, rods and wire, plates and sheet, and other zinc articles. It has 13 ten-digit lines with base rates from Free to 4.2%.
